changes.text: Install reef in Claude Code with two commands, and get `/reef:recall`, `/reef:remember` and `/reef:whats-new` alongside it. Your assistant also asks before anything that would overwrite or delete something, and stops asking to read.
Reef now uses its new brain-fan mark everywhere, from the app and website to favicons, social previews, and assistant connections.
The new brain-fan mark is now better balanced with the landing-page headline and navigation.

Inviting someone into a cove now reminds you that reef sends no email, so nothing reaches them until you pass the message on yourself. Previously the invite just reported success and the person you invited was never told.
The brain-fan mark now has clear edge space and a better-balanced size across reef's site, app, and shared previews.
The reef landing page now tells its story through a shared-memory conversation, clearer sections, and a shorter path to setup.
Links to reef now unfurl properly — share one in a chat, a post or a message and it arrives as a card instead of a bare address. The changelog has moved to reefwith.me/changelog.

While places are open for the launch, the reef home page now says so and invites you to take one. Once they're gone it goes back to explaining that you get in when someone already on reef invites you.
The reef website’s hero mark now has a richer seafoam-to-deep-teal gradient in both light and dark mode.

Connecting an assistant now shows reef's own approval page. Before you approve, it names where your sign-in will land and spells out plainly what a connected assistant can reach: everything you can read, write and manage in your coves.
The reef mark on the landing page now stands cleanly on the background without a decorative shape cutting across its base.
The reef website background now stays calm and clear without oversized decorative arcs competing with the content.
The reef website now carries its underwater character throughout, with gentle texture, currents, and more dimensional coves in light and dark mode.
reef can now tell you what's changed since you last looked. Open "What's new" from the account menu to see it.
reef now has terms of service, linked from every page's footer alongside the privacy policy and a changelog that actually opens.
